gen-amatic-sc-gf-noto-sans-gujarati: Amatic SC scrawls along in a single squeezed line, rustic and a bit quirky, with endings that stop well short of the stem. Noto Sans Gujarati is the sans-serif counterweight, its curved strokes finishing early and leaving generous room inside each letter.
gen-amatic-sc-gf-noto-sans-gunjala-gondi: Amatic SC looks like bent wire lettering, thin and constant. Its quirky hand is what it does best, while Noto Sans Gunjala Gondi, a plain sans with tall lowercase and cut-back terminals, handles the steady everyday text.
gen-amatic-sc-gf-noto-sans-gurmukhi: Noto Sans Gurmukhi reads crisp and businesslike. Amatic SC does casual, hand-lettered charm with no calligraphic shading to guide the eye, whereas the sans keeps its outward-pointing terminals tidy and ascenders low for steady, dependable text.
gen-amatic-sc-gf-noto-sans-hanunoo: Noto Sans Hanunoo fills most of the line height with lowercase and keeps its terminals open and easy going. Amatic SC brings the rustic sketchiness; this one brings the legibility.
gen-amatic-sc-gf-noto-sans-hebrew: Noto Sans Hebrew reads with a big midsection and wide gaps where curves meet stems. Amatic SC delivers rustic, rope-like roundness with walls as heavy as its straight lines, while the sans does the quiet, orderly work of carrying the text.
gen-amatic-sc-gf-noto-sans-hk: Rustic and quirky, Amatic SC bends its lines like tubing, and Noto Sans HK, a plain sans with large lowercase and brush ends lifted away before curves close, gives that bendy energy a clean, professional place to land. Its strongest quality is that tension between hand-made wobble and crisp text.
gen-amatic-sc-gf-noto-sans-imperial-aram: Noto Sans Imperial Aramaic reads approachable and professional, with a c whose ends point apart and capitals only a short step above lowercase. Amatic SC stays rustic and free of calligraphic modulation, and shrinking it small would thin that rope-like line even further.
gen-amatic-sc-gf-noto-sans-inscriptional: Tails and terminals as thick as the main stems give Amatic SC its rustic, quirky character. And Noto Sans Inscriptional Parthian, a sans with big open eyes and a deep middle band, supplies the pair's strongest quality: a hand-drawn voice sitting beside text that stays clear.
gen-amatic-sc-gf-noto-sans-jp: Hand-lettered rope, thin and outlined with no thick or thin parts, meets a very tall x-height in Noto Sans JP, a plain sans that sweeps its curves open. Side by side they feel like a sketchbook margin next to a tidy page.
gen-amatic-sc-gf-noto-sans-kaithi: Noto Sans Kaithi reads contemporary and plain, with an open channel in the e and lowercase that fills the line like capitals. Amatic SC does rustic, rod-stock lettering best, while this plain sans quietly carries the words.
